result:
**Idea in one sentence:** a stretch of shore seen from the air, where the time is a film of foam stranded in the grooves the backwash cut — the wave runs up over the whole glass at :00, churns the old time off the sand, and the draining water writes the new one in, while the foam figure rides the swell every second in between.

**Files** — only `sim/designs/beach-ds.js` (name "Swash", real blurb), plus renders in `out/`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `out/beach-ds-digits.png` | all ten digits (01:23 / 14:56 / 18:29) |
| `out/beach-ds.png` | the resting face |
| `out/beach-ds-turn.png` | `--sheet` across 10:09:58, 12 frames |
| `out/beach-ds-hour.png` | `--sheet` across 10:59:57, 12 frames over 9 s |
| `out/beach-ds.gif`, `out/beach-ds-hour.gif` | 300 frames / 6 s = 50 fps |
| `out/beach-ds-wear.png` | burn-in map |

**check.mjs: PASS** — 20160 frames, worst frame 12.65 ms of the 20 ms budget (79.1 fps allowed, design runs at 50), 0 frames over, 16.7 % of glass lit on average, hottest pixel (96,8) lit 19.5 h/day → ~2.4 years to half brightness. `frame()` is ~0.45 ms; a frame at an arbitrary time and a single isolated frame both render correctly.

**How it works.** The digits are hand-drawn centre-lines (a 21×23 box) baked into a *coverage field* with per-stroke taper and a slow width wobble, then rendered as a material: a solid heart opened by bubbles that multiply toward the edge, spray thrown past the ink. The field is sampled in the swell's own frame, so shape and texture bob together through ±1 px. The sea is two lines — the deep water's edge and the swash's leading edge — that sweep down the glass at the turn and drain back; the time is drawn only where the deep water has left the sand, so old and new are never on the glass together, and the reveal happens at the receding edge. The hour is a spring tide: the entire glass floods and holds, the drain is longer with deeper rills, and afterwards the waterline sits lower and creeps back over the next minutes.

**Honest weakest point.** The composition is still, at bottom, four centred digits with a beach drawn around them. At 32 rows there isn't room for the landscape to be more than a shoreline band, a swell arc or two and a whisper of grains, so the sea reads mostly as black until an event fires — the *scene* is thinner than the *mechanism* is good. The `2` is also the weakest of the ten (its bowl and diagonal crowd each other).
